meta.title: Developer Ownership Funding Stack Watchlist
meta.refresh_cadence: Quarterly review, or sooner when state/local ownership program terms change.
meta.commitment_note: Only awarded or committed sources may carry apply_to_gap=true. Available sources are context only.
meta.methodology: screening_apply means a source may appear as potential in screening displays and is never counted as committed funding; apply_to_gap counts toward closing a gap and requires awarded or committed status.
meta.deferral_note: A deferral is a carrying-cost benefit, not a TDC reduction.
meta.source_verification_note: Dollar and percentage fields are populated only when visible on a fetched, dated official source. Otherwise they remain null with verify=true.

programs.name: WMRHC Good Deeds buy-down
programs.capability_summary: Buy-down model that can reduce the for-sale price in exchange for a deed restriction.
programs.screening_note: Confirm buyer, unit, deed-restriction eligibility, and a project award before underwriting.
programs.benchmark_note: EPS Phase II Table 12 identifies deed restriction/buy-down as a developer-side affordability tool.
programs.source_note: WMRHC Good Deeds page read 2026-10-21: "The WMRHC will contribute 30% of the contracted purchase price to the purchase of a price-capped deed restriction on that property." The program buys a perpetual deed restriction from an eligible buyer household (an average of 1,400 work hours a year, at least 75% of them for a business located in Pitkin, West Eagle or Garfield County). The page caps the purchase price at $1,200,000 in Garfield County up valley of Glenwood Springs and $800,000 in the rest of Garfield County; its Pitkin County cap is printed as "$1,500,00" and needs confirming with WMRHC. The 30% is of the contract price; this screening applies 30% to development cost per unit, which is a modeling choice, not the program's basis. Project availability is not an award.

programs.name: Aspen affordable housing mitigation
programs.capability_summary: Local affordable-housing mitigation requirement that may affect project obligations or negotiated affordability terms.
programs.screening_note: Terms depend on project type, size, and local review; verify the current ordinance and fee schedule.
programs.benchmark_note: EPS Phase II Table 12 identifies inclusionary requirements as a developer-side affordability tool.
programs.source_note: Official City of Aspen page, re-opened 2026-10-21; it lists the adopted updates to affordable housing mitigation, the Housing Mitigation Fee-in-Lieu and FTE generation rates. Specific dollar terms are not encoded.

programs.name: CHFA down-payment assistance layering
programs.capability_summary: Buyer-side down-payment assistance that may layer when the buyer and mortgage path qualify.
programs.screening_note: Confirm CHFA loan, borrower, product eligibility, and an actual reservation before counting.
programs.benchmark_note: EPS Phase II Table 12 identifies down-payment assistance layering as a developer-side affordability tool.
programs.source_note: CHFA page read 2026-10-21: Second Mortgage Loan "Up to the lesser of $25,000 or 4 percent of your first mortgage", repayment deferred until certain events, such as payoff of the first mortgage, sale or refinance, or the home no longer being the borrower's primary residence; Down Payment Assistance Grant up to the lesser of $25,000 or 3 percent. Buyer-side availability is not a project source.

programs.name: DOLA Proposition 123 new construction / acquisition rehabilitation
programs.source_note: Official DOLA page fetched 2026-08-04 and rechecked 2026-10-26: "Urban & Rural/Resort $70,000/unit", "Up to 100% AMI", "Minimum of 30 years"; pre-applications are due 15 days before the first of each month. Fruita's jurisdiction filing does not constitute a project award.

programs.name: FHLBank Topeka Affordable Housing Program
programs.source_note: Official 2026 AHP page fetched 2026-08-04 and rechecked 2026-10-26; verifies $75,000 per unit and $1.5 million per project caps. The 2026 round is closed: "Round closing - July 31, 2026"; "Announcements - No later than Dec. 31, 2026".

programs.name: FHLBank Topeka Homeownership Set-Aside Program
programs.source_note: Official 2026 HSP page fetched 2026-08-04 and rechecked 2026-10-26; verifies 80% AMI, $15,000 maximum, $2,500 minimum, five-year retention, and member reservation workflow. Closed for 2026: reservations were accepted "through Sept. 30, 2026".

programs.name: CHFA construction financing for ownership development
programs.source_note: Official CHFA matrix fetched 2026-08-04 describes multifamily rental lending, not a confirmed for-sale construction product. Applicable primary for-sale product evidence is named by this candidate but has not been retrieved; amounts and terms remain null.
